summary_en: GAIA Inc. will acquire 150 ordinary shares of FP Bank Co., Ltd. (75% of 200 issued shares) and conduct a simplified share exchange to acquire the remaining 50 shares (25%), making FP Bank a wholly owned subsidiary. GAIA will issue 2,800 ordinary shares as consideration for the share exchange.
title_en: Notice Regarding Acquisition of FP Bank Co., Ltd. Shares and Complete Subsidiary Status Through Simplified Share Exchange
translation_en_brief:
GAIA Inc., a Tokyo-based independent financial advisor providing fee-based wealth management services, announced on 26 September 2026 that its board of directors resolved to acquire FP Bank Co., Ltd. and make it a wholly owned subsidiary through a combination of direct share acquisition and simplified share exchange. GAIA will acquire 150 ordinary shares (75% of FP Bank's 200 issued shares) through direct stock purchase and the remaining 50 shares (25%) through simplified share exchange. As consideration for the share exchange, GAIA will issue 2,800 newly created ordinary shares to FP Bank's shareholders. FP Bank, headquartered in Nihonbashi, Tokyo, is an IFA providing comprehensive financial consulting services through salaried financial planners. The company has recently been transitioning from an insurance-focused revenue model to one based on securities brokerage and fee-based services.

Both companies share a client-centric business philosophy centered on financial planning rather than product sales and are committed to employing advisors as full-time employees under a fee-based model. GAIA noted that FP Bank's proactive shift away from commission-based revenue aligns with GAIA's own earlier transition from commission-dependent structures. Since 2024, the companies have deepened their operational collaboration, with FP Bank acting as a financial product intermediary for fund wrap services on which GAIA provides investment advice. Post-acquisition, FP Bank founder and current representative director Masahiro Kubota is expected to continue leading the company. Both organizations will respect each other's corporate cultures and work environments, gradually deepening cooperation while building management foundations to support compliance and client-focused operations.
